$comment: What changed in each build (docs/RELEASES.md §3): a few short lines per version, newest first, shown on the launcher's version page and in the main menu's Versions card. Every release needs its entry: a client test fails when client/package.json's version has none, and the release script refuses to publish without one. Earlier entries were drafted from the merged pull requests' titles (2026-10-28).

changes: On phones and tablets, a Pick up button appears under the crosshair when you aim at a stick or rock: tap it to pick it up
Groundwork for smoother, cheaper water: the water's surface can now be described as a height map, ready for the renderer to draw (nothing changes on screen yet).
Sticks now lie on the ground under the trees, and stones gather at the feet of cliffs (a few on open grass too)
Aim at one and press E (X on a controller) to pick it up: they stack with the sticks and rocks that blocks drop
Picked-up ones stay gone in your world; break the ground under one and it tumbles loose
The versions page now keeps the newest build of the last 20 versions, plus the very first; every build stays on GitHub Releases
Other players now look like a proper animated character: a skinned, walking peasant in a sun hat, in the world's colours
Their walk speeds up when they sprint and settles to an idle sway when they stop, blending smoothly between
Standing still on a raft or any moving body no longer plays the walk: players stand still, for you and everyone watching
Walking on a moving body walks, even against its motion, and its footsteps keep pace
The big map's widest zoom shows the whole world, the island and all the sea round it, on any screen
No more square gaps in the sea on the big map: the ocean is drawn right out to the world's edge
The axe clears leaves: a swing goes through them, cutting them away with a rustle, and still chops the trunk behind
Leaves cleared in adventure drop sticks as they do when broken by hand
The big map has five zoom levels, from the minimap's area up close to the whole island; + and −, scroll, pinch or the controller step between them
Each level has its own detail, down to a metre a pixel, and is drawn once in the background and kept, so opening or zooming the map never waits
The map shows the ground's own colours again (sand is sand), lightly brighter on high ground
Axe cuts are real now: a notch is a V carved into the log, with fresh wood inside and kerfs as slits, lit and shadowed like the rest of the world
Moving blocks no longer shake as they fall, slide or fly: they glide smoothly whatever your frame rate or connection
A dynamite blast now destroys flying blocks inside its blast area, so chained dynamite no longer piles up debris pushed by several blasts
Adventure: sprinting, swimming and treading water tire you; run out of stamina and you can't sprint, swing the axe or stay afloat until you've caught your breath
Adventure: hold your breath under water; when your air runs out you start to drown until you surface
Stamina and air bars above the health bar while they aren't full (Settings, On screen hides them)
Yellow dynamite is half as strong again, and only cracks loose blocks with open air above or below them, not ones open only at their sides
Yellow dynamite's blast is half as strong again: its pieces fly at half the speed and players are knocked back half as far
The big map is a height map: ground coloured by its height, green lowlands through tans to grey and white peaks
Seas and lakes on the map are blue, darker where deeper; no more hill shading
The minimap's height shading setting now shows the same height colours
Behind the scenes: voxel model prototypes of the player, the wolf and the deer
Edited ground seen from far away keeps its grass instead of looking speckled with dirt
Rivers run twice as fast: their currents carry swimmers, rafts and the foam on them at double the speed
In the fastest reaches a swimmer can no longer make headway upstream
Behind-the-scenes test fix for the main menu's random background
The big map opens in a framed window over the game, with a close button, + and − zoom, Center on me and a scale bar
Drag to move it (or the controller's stick); scroll, pinch, + and −, or the triggers zoom; B, M or Esc closes it
The map is shaded by the ground's height: hills, valleys and slopes stand out, lit from the top left
The map explores everything near you, seen from above: valleys below a hilltop or a flight are no longer left blank
Ground the map has not seen up close takes its colours from the world's terrain, refined once you get near
In creative the big map shows the whole world: no fog, every hill, river and coast out to the horizon
Adventure keeps exploring: unvisited ground stays hidden
The main menu's turning views are seamless: no more joins in the sky or on the water
A Pause the look debug tool (F7, Settings → Debug) freezes clouds, water, plants and flames at one instant
The main menu's background is Random by default: a view picked at random that fades into another after each full turn
The main menu shows a slowly turning view of a real spot in a world: a beach, a river valley or a lake shore
Choose the view in Settings → On screen → Menu background
Settings opens from the main menu too, with every pane
In adventure, a hotbar slot you've used up shows an empty hand instead of the last block
The on-screen interface no longer overlaps itself on phones: the minimap, hotbar, status lines, flight slider and buttons each get their own place
On a phone the minimap is smaller and sits in the top corner, with the hotbar running up to it and scrolling when its items don't fit
The touch buttons sit in a compact block in the bottom right, clear of your held item
Hiding a part in Settings, On screen, lets the rest move into its place
Adventure players start with a stone axe
The stone axe swings with weight: a wind-up, a committed arc, a jolt when it bites and a looser follow-through when it misses
Swing any time; the axe's path is what it hits, and a line through the crosshair shows where it will pass
It is held the right way round, in two grips for level and vertical swings, with a flint-grey head
Notches look cut: fresh tan wood inside, deepening as you chop; stone and dirt just clank
A tree creaks and leans as it nears the fall, and leaves drift down with each hit
Other players see the axe in your hands
Distant terrain is sharper by default: Distant detail starts at 3 in every preset and on phones
A round minimap in the top corner: turns with you, shows the ground, water and other players
Press M (or tap the minimap) for a map of everywhere you have explored: scroll to zoom, drag to pan
Settings, On screen: hide the minimap, or turn its height shading off
A felled tree no longer throws you far away when it falls on you
The stone axe is on the creative hotbar
Your chops show: notches and cuts in the trunk, and wood chips fly off each swing
Level and vertical swings of the axe in your hands
A felled tree now falls toward your notch, like real felling: stand clear
In Adventure, logs need an axe: hands can't break them (leaves and plants still break by hand)
Adventure runs as smoothly as Creative again: dropped items lying on the ground no longer make the shadows redraw over and over
A stone axe: hold it and left click to chop a tree, right click to switch between level and vertical swings
Aim matters: chop into the trunk, then a little above or below to knock the chunk out; hacking one spot is slow
Cut a little past halfway and the tree falls, away from your notch
On the ground, chop a log across with vertical swings: each length you cut through drops wood in Adventure
Adventure: blocks you break drop items; walk near them to pick them up
Placing a block in Adventure uses one from your hotbar, which now shows how many you have
Grass drops dirt and sometimes a rock, leaves drop sticks, tall grass drops seeds and now and then a gem
Gems go to your wallet (up to 99), shown by the hotbar; E opens your backpack to move items around
Dying in Adventure drops what you carry; loose items vanish after 5 minutes. Creative is unchanged
Behind-the-scenes fixes so the automated checks pass again
No change to how the game plays
Settings you haven't changed now follow the game's defaults, so improved defaults reach you
A setting you changed shows a ↺ button: press it to go back to the default
A chosen graphics preset is remembered, and updates to it reach you; changing one of its settings shows Custom
Settings saved by earlier versions are kept as they are; Reset sets everything back to the defaults
Game modes: a new world is Creative or Adventure (experimental), chosen when you create it
Creative is as before, with no damage at all: no fall, blast or crush damage
Adventure: falls, blasts and falling pieces hurt; no flight and no brush tools
Your existing worlds stay Creative
Water Low is now see-through, with light rippling on it, and much lighter on phones
Water High is merged into Medium, which keeps the whole look; a saved High plays as Medium
Water's moving light patterns are redrawn every other frame, a little cheaper everywhere
Settings are split into Graphics, Sound, Gameplay and On screen, one compact column each
A Preset slider in Graphics: Low, Mobile, Medium, High and Ultra; change any one setting and it reads Custom
New players draw at 50 % resolution, upscaled, for a much smoother frame; a render scale you set is kept
Phones start on Mobile, computers on High
Sun rays are much stronger, and the moon casts visible rays too
Fixes the last three releases, which failed to build
Torches glow softly in the air at night and in caves, with faint rays past what stands before them
The Light shafts setting covers them: Low draws fewer, Off none
The waterline band is smooth instead of speckled, at any render scale
Sun rays through trees and clouds are a little longer and softer
Soft sun rays through gaps in trees, clouds and hills, and faint moon rays at night
Under water, sunlight shafts fan down from the surface and flicker with its ripples
Snell's window glows a bright white-cyan with a soft edge
A new Light shafts setting in Graphics: High, Low or Off
The waterline band is half as thick and smoother
From under the water the surface overhead shows broken bright cells with darker gaps, brightest toward the sun, fading softly into the deep blue instead of ending at a hard line
The waterline's band ripples more, its reflection of the land is blurred by the waves, and its dark edge no longer looks jagged
Your own shadow no longer leaves a faint smudge on the water beside you
Stepping through the hotbar with the arrow keys or a swipe now makes the hotbar's click
The waterline is a straight, wavy line that glides smoothly up and down the screen as you sink or rise, instead of a curved arc that jumped
Along it, the water's surface is now a band you can see: a dark edge over a bright line, rippled and coloured by the view around it
From under the water the surface shows a rippled texture, mirrors the water below and opens onto the sky through a window overhead
No more dark blotch of your own shadow on the water beside you
No change in the game: a measured breakdown of what the water costs, and a plan for cheaper water that stays pretty
The bright line where the water meets your view is a little thicker
A clean waterline: with your eye at the surface the view splits along a crisp, gently wavy line, the world above and the water below, with a thin bright edge between.
Clearer water underneath: the blue haze starts a few metres out and thins, so you can see the sandy floor and its caustics far away.
Smoother big blasts: a chain of dynamite shares one budget of smoke and dust, and the smoke is cheaper to draw, so eight charges by a river no longer drop the frame rate.
Smoother dynamite: flying debris no longer makes the distant shadows redraw every frame, so a chain of blasts drops far fewer frames.
Smoother flying over new terrain: loading the world now fits around each frame instead of taking a fixed slice on top of it.
Standing still costs less: the distant terrain isn't re-chosen every frame when nothing has changed.
Measured why flying over new terrain drops frames on a MacBook Air: the main thread's work on arriving chunks, not the GPU.
A dev link setting, ?workers=N, sets how many background workers generate and mesh the world, for testing.
Settings, Graphics: Render scale draws the world at 75, 67 or 50 % of the screen's resolution for a faster frame (100 % by default)
Settings, Graphics: Upscaler picks how it fills the screen: Stretch (cheapest, softer) or Sharpen (an edge-aware upscale and sharpening)
Plans: a note on pre-computing big explosions' physics for a future version
Yellow dynamite cracks loose only blocks that were touching air: buried blocks around the crater stay put
Yellow dynamite's blast is half as strong: its pieces fly at half the speed and players are knocked back half as far
Yellow dynamite cracks loose exposed ground out to 7 m (was 5 m); it still destroys 4 m
Behind the scenes: measured what each feature costs a frame on a MacBook Air, to find what to speed up first (nothing changes in play)
Behind the scenes: measured the game natively and in Chrome on a full Retina screen with every effect on high (nothing changes in play)
Behind the scenes: a native Mac test harness to measure how the game runs outside the browser (nothing changes in play)
Water shields what is behind it: dynamite no longer destroys or throws blocks on the far side of water
Dynamite touching water no longer destroys or throws blocks: it just makes its wave, knockback and damage
The performance line shows frames drawn out of the screen's frames (e.g. 38/60 fps), and how many were skipped waiting on the graphics card
Yellow dynamite now visibly cracks: every block it exposed to air breaks loose with the blast's push, and the rest of its outer shell flies wherever it has a way out, as red's does
New compatibility line: worlds and servers from 0.49.x builds can't be shared with 0.50
Leaves under water are flooded: no more flickering water faces or foam round them
From now on, a block property added by a newer version or a mod stays on the block in older 0.50 builds
Stirred water no longer slowly gains or loses water as it settles
Explosion smoke and dust now billow out the open side: out of a cliff face, down from a cave roof
Yellow dynamite: clears 4 m and cracks the rock around it that touches air, which crumbles and falls
Set under a cave roof, it brings the roof down
The left and right arrow keys step the hotbar one slot at a time
Swiping sideways on a touchpad steps the hotbar too
Touchpad scrolling no longer skips several slots at once
Dynamite set off in or beside water now makes waves that run to the banks and bounce back
Floating pieces and swimmers ride the waves
Blue dynamite: a 4 m blast that clears everything in it and throws nothing
Green dynamite: clears 4 m and flings the ground round it out to 5 m, like red's
Dynamite set flush in the ground blows a real crater and throws its debris clear instead of dropping it back in
Dynamite's blast is 5 m again, with twice the force
Dynamite blasts out through the open side: up from the ground, out of a cliff face, down from a cave roof
Rock a blast would only drive into more rock stays put, so a blast throws about half as many pieces; buried dynamite leaves a cavity
A river running through still water no longer sends ripples back through it, so a filled pond behind a dam can go still
A river no longer slows down right next to a block you place on its bank
Teleporting or respawning into the hills no longer stalls the game for a moment
Dynamite's blast is smaller again (4 m) but throws its pieces and players half again as hard
Big blasts no longer slow the game for as long
Behind the scenes: measured why the full reservoir behind a dam never settles, and added the tests that reproduce it (no change to play yet)
Behind the scenes: checked that autosaving in the browser doesn't stall the game (a few milliseconds at most), and pinned how the server treats an empty chunk request
Dynamite is bigger: its blast reaches 5 m, destroys the blocks within 2 m outright and throws the rest out as pieces
A blast now hurts only players within 2 m of it; farther off it just knocks you back
The game runs faster in the browser, most of all in a big dynamite blast: it now uses the browser's WebAssembly SIMD
A browser too old for that now says so, naming the versions that work, instead of showing a blank page
Moving around the world no longer hitches as new terrain comes into view: the work that decides which chunks are empty sky now runs in the background
Your world's autosave no longer causes a hitch: it is written a little at a time between moments of play
A dynamite blast keeps the game smooth: no more stutters while its pieces fly
Your world keeps running closer to full speed after a big blast, as water refilling the crater no longer rebuilds the ground's collision
A big dynamite blast no longer freezes the screen for over half a second as its pieces fly
Pieces floating in water after a blast cost the world less to simulate
Dynamite: place it, then light it with a torch held against it; after its fuse it blows, flinging every block around it
A blast knocks back and hurts anyone near it (standing on it is fatal), sets off other dynamite nearby and blows water out
Explosions flash, throw up smoke and dust, boom (quieter far away) and shake the view; each can be turned off in Settings → Explosions
Many falling pieces at once no longer freeze the screen for seconds
Waterfalls: water pouring over a drop, such as a notch cut in a dam, now falls as a sheet with foam and spray where it lands
A waterfall pushes you down and away from it, and can't be swum or jumped up; floating logs and rafts under one are pushed too
Each waterfall rushes, louder the more water it carries and the nearer you are
Settings → Water → Waterfalls turns the falling sheets off
The loading screen lists what it is doing as the game starts, each step with its time, so a slow one shows
The game's download shows in MB, and shaping a new world's map counts its faces
A new world starts a little sooner: its file opens while the world map is still being shaped
Sand undercut in a dig falls down at once and is blocks again in a few seconds, instead of hanging in the air for half a minute
Collapses and heaps of falling pieces cost the world far less time, so the game stays smooth while they fall
Fixed a crash when a ramp was placed deep underground
Brushes work in every world now, not just the sandbox (V turns them on)
Brushes reach 256 m, and always show where they will act, even aimed at the sky or at unloaded ground
Block, selection and brush outlines stay the same width on screen, so far ones are easy to see
Behind the scenes: faster turnaround on fixes (the project's working rules)
Ground you have built on or dug no longer looks terraced from far away
Distant terrain still being updated when the world saves is updated when you return
The river below a dam now dries up completely, down to where the next stream joins it, in saved worlds too
Water left in a dip of the dry riverbed stays there, still
Rivers no longer seem to stop on their level stretches: a reach that lies flat runs as fast as the river around it
The flow on rivers now shows as far out as it is drawn, not stopping 30 to 50 m away
Water no longer stands on top of a dam and pours off it for ever: once the dam is higher than the river, what covered it drains away, in saved worlds too
Falls of up to 10 m never hurt; past that the damage climbs quickly, and a 20 m fall is lethal
Slow creeks show their flow too: faint foam and drifting flecks start on water moving at a walking crawl, not only on fast rivers
No more triangle-shaped holes in the water where a river steps up to its next pool
A dam across a river raises the water behind it again, on level stretches too, and the river below it drops
Rivers run on their level and shallow stretches: swimmers and boats drift downstream there
Worlds saved before are fixed when loaded
Sliding up a ramp launches you off its top on your own momentum, at the ramp's angle, instead of holding you to the top and sending you off its far edge flat
Sliding down a hill keeps you on the ramps instead of bouncing you off each edge
Falls of 5 m or less never hurt; past that the damage climbs quickly, and a 12 m fall is lethal
In the air you keep your speed: letting go or steering no longer slows you, and holding a direction turns you instead
Walking no longer adds on top of a knockback's speed
Foam on running water no longer shows as white circles: the streaks are thin dashes along the current
Drifting flecks are small ragged scraps of foam, drawn out along the flow, fading in and out, fewer in slow water and lit like the water at dusk
Holding Place builds on into water: a line or a floor dragged under water, or out from the shore, no longer stops after its first block
Testing tools can find places by what is there: the nearest sea, river, deep water or dry land, and look down a river along its current
The water benchmarks find the sea and a river wherever the terrain puts them
Damming a river no longer makes the game hitch in its first seconds: distant views of the flooded land update a little later, and new terrain is made on its own thread in your own worlds
Water runs on a thread of its own: damming a river or flooding a pit no longer makes the game stop and start
Floods and drains run at full speed again instead of slowing down when much water moves
Water that rises over a steep slope fills the bottom half of the slope too, and leaves it when the water goes
A performance line under the status line shows what holds a frame back: frames drawn a second, the CPU's and the GPU's time per frame, and the server's ticks
Every part of the screen (the status line, hotbar, crosshair, health, flight speed and more) can be hidden under Settings, On screen, and stays as you left it; on a phone the menu button always shows
The frame rate in the status line counts only the frames actually drawn: a phone whose graphics fall behind showed 60 while it drew 30
Water is much cheaper to draw up close: looking down into a river on Medium took about a quarter less of the frame, and on High about a third less
Phones draw slightly cheaper reflections on Medium
You can see which way water flows: ripples are carried along with the current, pale foam streaks run with fast water, and small flecks drift downstream
Each one can be turned off under Settings, Water
Damming a river no longer makes the game stop and start: while a lot of water is moving it flows a little slower instead
Less network traffic for river currents, so joining a world near water loads its terrain sooner
Fall damage now counts only how fast you're falling: running or sliding fast into a slope never hurts
Landing on a slope softens a fall: the steeper the slope, the less it hurts
A fast slide carries up steep ramps and launches off their tops; slopes now speed up and slow down a slide by plain gravity
Walking into a steep ramp no longer stops you like a wall: you get a little way up and slide back
Dying on the underside of the world no longer turns the camera upside down
Rivers no longer show flat blue sheets behind their steps when you look upstream
Rivers now have a current: they carry swimmers and floating rafts downstream, faster where they fall steeply
Water you set moving does too, such as a lake let out through a cut or a dammed river let go
On slow devices, a quick tap of jump is no longer lost, and holding Place builds on more reliably when walking back or crouch-jumping a tower
Landing on a slope never hurts: only hard landings on flat ground do
Letting go of sprint in the air no longer slows you down: sprint and crouch don't change your speed mid-air
Hold crouch as you land while moving fast and you slide, with or without sprint
Sliding down a steep slope with crouch held carries on as a slide where the ground levels out
Ramps make real jumps: fast enough, you fly off a ramp's top or a downhill edge instead of sticking to the ground
Play worlds from older versions: pick a newer version on the Versions page and confirm the warning to play a copy or upgrade
Water's behaviour (how rough riverbeds are, how fast water calms and sleeps, how far an edit wakes it) now comes from one settings file, ready for tuning
Rivers no longer have dirt walls sticking out into them where they step down: the water simply falls to the next pool
Where a river joins a lower one, it runs down to it in a stream instead of standing as a wall of water
A new compatibility line: worlds saved in 0.48 open in 0.48 builds
Water is now simulated as a surface that flows from column to column: dams back rivers up, cut lakes drain, floods spread by one law
Rivers and lakes as generated stay exactly as they are until you change them, and cost nothing while they rest
Moving water calms and goes to sleep within seconds of settling
Spilled water always flows downhill to the lowest place nearby, and pools where it can't go lower
A flood pours over a river's banks into the river below instead of spreading along them
Water overflowing a dam shows standing over the dam's top
Rivers are now planned as a chain of pools and steps, so water stays where it was made and moves only where you can see it
Steep mountain streams run as chutes of flowing water instead of stacks of tiny pools
A dam's effect travels on down the river, even through country nobody has visited
No more invisible walls holding water up: gaps in a riverbank spill and pool beside it
New world terrain: worlds from earlier versions open in their own version
Water only fills a pool where you can see it pour in: no more pools filling from nowhere
Below a dam the river drains to standing pools until the dam spills over
River steps are walled all the way across, so water no longer stands in walls beside lower water
Water rising over a slope now fills the ramps under it
New world terrain: worlds from earlier versions open in their own version
Copy block info now includes the world's last block edits, to help reproduce reported bugs
Creeks pour through narrower gaps at their steps, closer to the water they carry
New world terrain: worlds from earlier versions open in their own version
The river below a dam stays at its level all the way down, rapids included, instead of rising
A pool below a filling dam no longer drains dry and comes back at another level
A dam no longer makes the river just below it rise as much: the dammed river's water is no longer counted twice
Rivers are shaped so their water stays at rest by the same physics as any other water
River steps have a lip that the water pours through, and pour as a slope down to the next pool
Waterfalls reach all the way down to the water below
A dammed river fills and pours over the dam without rising higher than it should
New world terrain: worlds from earlier versions open in their own version
Water flows through flooded ramps: a dammed river rises up its banks and pours over the dam
Rivers stay at rest where part of them loads in later
Dev links: ?fresh=1 starts a local world over from its seed, ?at=x,y,z starts you at a point
Rising water no longer vanishes for a moment and reappears higher at each step: it now rises smoothly
Water on the slopes along a shore rises with the pool instead of sitting at the full block
A pool whose level sits right at a step no longer flickers between two heights
The block info copy (F6) now includes the water around you in a local world, to help track down water problems
A dam across a river now holds it back: the river rises behind it and pours over, instead of draining away unseen
Water spilling over a wide edge, like a flood over a low bank, now pours down the slope instead of sitting as a still sheet
Far-off water fills smoothly too, meeting the nearby water's surface without a step
Water fills and drains smoothly instead of jumping half a block at a time
A new compatibility line: worlds saved in 0.44 open in 0.44 builds
Damming or releasing a river reaches players far downstream, travelling down the river at its own pace
Rivers rise and fall with the water reaching them: a river below a filling dam runs low until it spills
A dam keeps filling and a cut lake keeps draining after you walk away, until the water settles
Water held back out of reach no longer sends its full river downstream meanwhile
Dams, floods and drained lakes are saved with the world and come back as you left them after a restart
Water you leave behind catches up when you return: a dam filling while you were away is full and spilling
A dam's flood now goes on up the river as you travel there, instead of stopping where the world had loaded
Editing the river beyond a flood no longer drains it
Holes in a dam let water through by their size and the depth of water behind them, instead of draining it
Two pools joined by a small opening even out over time; a wide gap still makes one body of water
Water pours over a sill and through openings by one realistic pressure law
A wall across a river raises the water behind it until it spills over, even a wall level with the water
Water spilling over a wall or through a cut is drawn running down the other side
The river below a wall keeps its level instead of filling with the spill
New worlds: slopes at the edge of rivers and lakes hold water, so the water no longer ends in a wall
A new compatibility line: worlds from 0.42 keep opening in 0.42
Rivers and lakes stay as they are until you change them: a block in a riverbed no longer floods or drains the river
Rivers carry the world map's flow, so a dam fills at the river's real rate and the river below it runs low
Water out of reach, or beside unloaded ground, waits instead of flooding or vanishing
Slopes at the water's edge fill with water when the water reaches them
Blocks placed in a riverbed no longer flood a waterfall and then drain the river dry
A flood over a river's steps leaves each step its pool when it goes down
Water flows: dam a river and it fills up and spills over the dam
Cut through a lake's shore and it drains down to the cut; dig a deeper trench and the river follows it
Cut into the sea from lower ground and the sea floods in up to its own level
Days are 20 minutes long in new worlds, and each world keeps its own day length
A new compatibility line: worlds and servers from 0.41 don't mix with 0.42
You push like a person: a single log slides along the ground at a slow walk, stone stays put
Rafts glide through the water when you let go instead of stopping dead
Standing or landing on a floating raft presses it down under your weight
Pushing keeps you up against what you push, smooth with lag too
Pushing a floating raft is smooth: your game predicts the push instead of correcting you
Objects next to you are drawn where they really are now, so you no longer sink into them
Heavy things resist your push by their weight: a big raft moves slowly, a heavy log on land not at all
Falling blocks settle once and stay where they land
You can push floating objects, however heavy
Slowly drifting objects no longer freeze on screen
Standing on a floating object no longer makes your character twitch
The hover outline on a moving object's block lines up with it
The build platform is now ground you build on: blocks placed on it make a moving object, held still while you build
Blocks you place touching the object join it, by click or by dragging
Break the platform out from under it to set the object free
Build platforms drag in Line and Flat mode like any block
Moving objects float: a raft of wood floats and rights itself, stone sinks
Falling trees that land in a lake float
Build platform: place one and build onto it to make a moving object (a raft, a cart) that never settles into the ground
Moving objects are saved with your world, and players who join see them
Falling trees and sand in progress show for players who join mid-fall
Break blocks off falling trees and sand while they're still moving; a break through one splits it in two
Aim at a moving piece to outline the block you'll break
A new compatibility line: worlds and servers from 0.40 don't mix with 0.41
Lots of falling blocks at once (sand, trees) no longer freeze and jump: every one keeps moving smoothly
Steering on steep slides is back to how it was
Slides carry on down stepped hills and last a little longer on flat ground
You stop a little sooner when you let go of the movement keys
Jumping out of a slide is always at least a full jump, angled out from the slope
Steep slides are harder to steer and to slow down, like a classic slide trap
Jumping out of a slide on any slope pushes you out from the slope and adds to your speed: fast and low downhill, high and slower uphill
Bridging only builds while you look below the horizon; looking up stops it, and its outline only shows where it would build
Stone slopes in the hotbar: a shallow one and a steep one, placed with the uphill side facing where you look
Hold place to build a run of slopes
Crouching in the air no longer slows you down
Landing with crouch held while moving slides on, from a fall or a jump out of a slide
Jumping off a steep slope pushes you out from its face and adds to your speed
Very tall trees and columns tip over from their base instead of flipping out
Trees on the underside of the world fall away from you, not toward you
